title: Qt: Add Find in Packet search feature follow-up
description:
This is a follow-up to !25004.

## MR contains

Three commits:

1. Reapply the original feature (reverts e420dd3af4)
2. Stratoshark: Fix startup crash by properly initializing proto_container\_ before proto_tree\_ (fixup 7cb0b8bf)
3. Qt: Align Find in Packet toolbar UI with Find Packet toolbar

## Feedback addressed ([view here](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25004#note_3393113460))

**Stig (1) Why second find?**

* The existing Find Packet bar searches across all packets in the capture file. Find in Packet searches only within the selected packet's protocol tree, counting and navigating multiple field matches within a single packet. These are distinct use cases.

**Stig (2) UI looks different / unfinished**

* Fixed. Pill-style toggle buttons replaced with a QComboBox (String / Regular Expression) and QCheckBox (Case sensitive), matching the existing Find Packet toolbar controls exactly as well as the style of the search box. (Checked again on using MacOS)

**Stig (3) What does the Find in Packet checkbox do?**

* The checkbox in the Find Packet bar is a toggle that opens only the main window Find In Packet menu and closes every instance of the Find In Packet menu. Providing a single entry point for both features from the same toolbar.

**Stig (4) Confusing names**

* This was done on purpose: Find Packet = search across packets in the capture, Find in Packet = search within the fields of the currently selected packet.

**Stig (5) Pop-out window: menu item does not open bar in pop-out**

* The Ctrl+Alt+F shortcut toggles the Find in Packet bar within a pop-out window when that window is focused. The Edit menu item is intentionally scoped to the main window only, it toggles the Find in Packet checkbox in the Find Packet bar but does not close pop-out window bars, which is expected behavior. The shortcut is the intended method for controlling the find bar in pop-out windows.

**Stig (6) No visible way to open find bar in pop-out window**

* The Ctrl+Alt+F shortcut works when tabbed into the pop-out window and toggles that window's own find bar independently. This was verified in the original testing and remains functional. As well as the shortcut being labeled in the 'Edit' toolbar dropdown.

**Stig (7) Red on no-match is inconsistent**

* Fixed. Red background now indicates invalid input or invalid regex only, consistent with Find Packet.

**Stig (8) No green background after reopening with a match**

* Fixed. Syntax state is now evaluated on each search execution.

**Stig (9) Up/down buttons do not work initially**

* Fixed. Match state is computed on open, not deferred until an option is toggled.

**Stig (10) UI alignment with Find Packet**

* Fixed. Included within newest commit.

**Stig (11) Documentation**

* Release notes in doc/Wireshark_Release_Notes.adoc

**Michael Mann Stratoshark crash**

* Fixed. Included within newest commit.

* The background color of the find is wrong, it has too much space and the Cancel button has wrong size. This must look the same as the main find.
* The back and forward icons are not the same logic as in the main find, which has "Backwards" checkbox and a "Find" button. I think we should use common UX in this two places.

The background and foreground colour issues in the screenshots are not a bug in this MR, that is #21317

1. I added a User Guide section in doc/wsug_src/wsug_work.adoc under Finding Packets.
 2. Fixed: the checkbox is disabled when no single packet is selected, and enabling in-packet mode without a selection is blocked. Selection loss also clears in-packet mode so you don’t search or highlight with an invalid tree context.
 3. Moved Find in selected Packet next to Multiple occurrences on the options row.
 4. Changed the name: "Find in selected Packet"
 5. Backwards is intentionally disabled in in-packet mode (navigation uses Enter/Shift+Enter and Find instead). Fixed the bug where it stayed disabled after turning off Find in selected Packet.
 6. Removed Edit -\> Find in Packet from the main window Edit menu. The main window now uses only the Find Packet toolbar and the Find in selected Packet checkbox for in-packet search. 
 7. Added a checkbox 'Find in Packet' options row rather than a separate bottom Find button. The checkbox tooltip shows the shortcut and you can still use the Close button to toggle the menu.
 8. The pop-out find bar now uses the same Find and Cancel QPushButtons as the main Find Packet toolbar, with prev/next icon buttons removed.
 9. The pop-out bar now has the main pattern: Find + Cancel, Enter/Shift+Enter for next/previous match, instead of separate back/forward icons.
10. Reordered it to match the main toolbar.
11. The status bar counter (n of m/no matches) is in place for Find in Packet on the main window. Something similar for the Find Packet options would need extra match indexing the current find APIs don’t provide, could follow up on that separately if its nessesary.

+==== Finding Text in the Selected Packet
+
+[#ChWorkFindInSelectedPacketSection]
+
+When exactly one packet is selected in the packet list, the
+<<ChWorkFindPacketToolbar,"Find Packet" toolbar>> can search within that
+packet's protocol tree instead of searching the whole capture file.
+
+Check btn:[Find in selected Packet] on the options row at the bottom of
+the toolbar. Wireshark limits the search type to btn:[String] and
+btn:[Regular Expression] and searches only the packet details of the
+currently selected packet. The btn:[Search in], btn:[Multiple
+occurrences], and btn:[Search backward] options are not used in this
+mode.
+
+Enter a search string or regular expression in the search field, then
+click btn:[Find] or press kbd:[Enter] to move to the next match.
+Press kbd:[Shift+Enter] to move to the previous match. You can also use
+menu:Edit[Find Next] (kbd:[Ctrl+N]) and menu:Edit[Find Previous]
+(kbd:[Ctrl+B]). Matching fields are highlighted in the protocol tree.
+
+While a search is active, the status bar can show a match counter such
+as `[3 of 57]` before the description of the selected field. If no
+matches are found, Wireshark shows a message in the status bar.
+
+btn:[Find in selected Packet] is available only when a single packet is
+selected. If the selection is cleared or includes more than one packet,
+the checkbox is disabled and any in-packet highlighting is removed.
+Click btn:[Cancel] on the toolbar or press kbd:[Esc] to close the Find
+Packet toolbar and clear the highlighting.
+
+==== Finding Text in the Single-Packet Window
+
+[#ChWorkFindInPacketDialogSection]
+
+When you view a packet in a separate window (see
+<<ChWorkPacketSepView>>), you can search within that window's protocol
+tree without using the main Find Packet toolbar.
+
+Check btn:[Find in Packet] in the row of options below the protocol
+tree, or select menu:Edit[Find in Packet] (kbd:[Ctrl+Alt+F]). Wireshark
+opens a find bar above the protocol tree. The find bar provides
+btn:[String] and btn:[Regular Expression] search, a btn:[Case sensitive]
+option, a match counter, and btn:[Find] and btn:[Cancel] buttons.
+
+Enter a search string or regular expression, then click btn:[Find] or
+press kbd:[Enter] to move to the next match. Press kbd:[Shift+Enter] to
+move to the previous match. Matching fields are highlighted in the
+protocol tree. Uncheck btn:[Find in Packet] or click btn:[Cancel] to
+close the find bar and clear the highlighting.
